articles.title: “Brexit hasn’t worked and Britain lost more that it gained” says Andy Burnham | BBC News
articles.titleZh: 安迪·伯纳姆表示：“英国脱欧没有奏效，英国的损失大于收获” | BBC新闻
articles.summary:
British PM Andy Burnham has said the UK has lost more than it has gained from leaving the European Union in a speech ahead of a UK-EU summit later this week.

Speaking at the Lord Mayor's Banquet in London, Andy Burnham compared the UK's Brexit deal to the "emperor's new clothes" - saying "a needlessly hard Brexit" had created barriers for businesses and the promise to "take back control" was not delivered.

He is due to sign new agreements on food, energy and youth mobility with the bloc at the summit, after the substance of those deals was set by his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

The opposition Conservatives have said Labour are "dragging us into the European Union via the back door".

In his first major speech on foreign policy, the prime minister said that following the summit he would begin new discussions with the EU about options for "our long-term relationship".  However, he warned it would take time and insisted that "at every stage the British people will be the boss".  Burnham has ruled out major changes before the next general election.

On the UK's current relationship with EU, Burnham said: "It's like the emperor's new clothes – where no-one is prepared to say the obvious truth. Well, I say it as I see it. And to be frank, the emperor has nothing on. "The Brexit we were given has not worked. We have lost more than we have gained."

Ahead of Friday's UK-EU summit, Burnham set out three tests for any agreement. Firstly, that it must be consistent with Labour's 2024 general election manifesto pledge that there would be "no return to the single market, the customs union, or freedom of movement".  He also said it must improve the original Brexit deal and bring it closer to what people thought they were voting for in 2016. Finally, he said any deal must pass the "Makerfield test" of providing tangible improvements to people's everyday lives - a reference to voters in Burnham's Greater Manchester constituency.

The Prime Minister also said the prospect of a new deal is a "win-win" and illustrates a "new approach". He said "Britain was back in the game in a big way" and would be a country that "leads with its values".

Sophie Raworth presents BBC News at Ten reporting by James Landale.

articles.readingTextZh:
英国首相安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）在本周晚些时候举行的英欧峰会前发表讲话时表示，英国从脱离欧盟中损失的要多于获得的。

安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）在伦敦市长晚宴上发言时，将英国的脱欧协议比作“皇帝的新衣”，称“不必要的硬脱欧”给企业造成了障碍，而“收回控制权”的承诺也未能兑现。

在峰会上，他将与欧盟签署有关粮食、能源和青年流动的新协议，这些协议的实质内容已由他的前任基尔·斯塔默爵士确定。

反对党保守党表示，工党正在“通过后门将我们拉回欧盟”。

在关于外交政策的首次重要讲话中，首相表示，在峰会结束后，他将与欧盟就“我们长期关系”的各种方案展开新一轮讨论。

不过，他警告称这需要时间，并坚持认为“在每个阶段，英国人民都将是主导者”。

伯纳姆已排除在下一次大选前进行重大改革的可能性。

对于英国目前与欧盟的关系，伯纳姆表示：“这就像《皇帝的新装》——没有人愿意说出显而易见的真相。

好吧，我只是实话实说。

坦白说，皇帝根本没穿衣服。“我们得到的脱欧方案没有奏效。

我们的损失大于收获。”

在周五的英欧峰会召开之前，伯纳姆为任何协议提出了三项检验标准。

首先，它必须与工党2024年大选宣言的承诺一致，即“不会重返单一市场、关税同盟或人员自由流动”。

articles.title: What is the UK government's plan to create more jobs for young people? | BBC Newscast
articles.titleZh: 英国政府计划如何为年轻人创造更多就业机会？| BBC Newscast
articles.summary:
Today, we discuss more details about Alan Milburn’s review into young people and work, which will be published on Tuesday.  

The report will call for a gradual lowering of National Insurance paid by firms on employing under-25s. Adam is joined by Chris Mason and business editor Simon Jack to unpack what impact these proposed changes might have.

Also, the UK’s relationship with the EU is being discussed again ahead of a UK-EU summit this week. Chris and Adam assess the lines we expect to hear from Andy Burnham speaking at Lord Mayor's Banquet on Monday. 

00:00 Intro
01:25 How the government has handled the Alan Milburn review
03:18 The three phases of the Milburn preview
04:12 Plans to lower employers' National Insurance for young people
07:12 How much does it cost to hire a young person?
10:52 The opposition's response to the plans
12:13 What will happen to the Milburn report?
16:42 The prime minister's Lord Mayor's Banquet speech and the EU summit
18:31 The prime minister's three rules for dealing with the EU
28:22 Russell Brand's message from prison

articles.title: ‘Out of the Iranian playbook’: Security experts react to DC bomb plot
articles.titleZh: “出自伊朗的剧本”：安全专家对华盛顿爆炸阴谋的反应
articles.summary:
New US intelligence indicates that Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or a chemical weapon in Washington, DC, even as officials continue to debate whether Iran can or will attempt to execute such a plot, according to seven US officials.

Iranian plotting against current and former US officials, including a murder-for-hire plot against Trump in 2024, has been ongoing since the president’s first administration and largely concentrated on opportunities to kill US officials while they were traveling overseas.

CNN talks to national security experts to break down the plot.

0:00 What are Iran’s capabilities?
2:18 How likely is Iran to follow though on this?
4:50 How would a dirty bomb work?
7:01 Quigley: This threat is “very serious”
8:26 Is Iran pursuing this as retaliation for intensifying the war?

Watch 24/7 live news with CNN Headlines: https://bit.ly/4eIvlTr

Stream more on CNN with an All Access subscription: https://cnn.it/4AZMu54

#News #iran #dc

articles.title: Airline and bank outages, ground stop, Microsoft blackout: What’s behind them?
articles.titleZh: 航空公司和银行系统瘫痪、航班停飞、微软系统宕机：背后原因是什么？
articles.summary: Cybersecurity expert Alex Hamerstone tells CNN’s Erin Burnett that the recent string of ground stops, United Airlines, banking, and Microsoft outages isn’t the work of a single bad actor. Instead, the TrustedSec director points to growing reliance on complex, aging systems and companies “not testing things prior to rolling them out.”
articles.summaryZh: 直接播放媒体官方频道发布的新闻视频，保留记者原声、现场声音及原始语速。
articles.sourceNote: Official publisher video · original English audio
articles.readingText:
Cybersecurity expert Alex Hamerstone tells CNN’s Erin Burnett that the recent string of ground stops, United Airlines, banking, and Microsoft outages isn’t the work of a single bad actor.

Instead, the TrustedSec director points to growing reliance on complex, aging systems and companies “not testing things prior to rolling them out.”
articles.readingTextZh:
网络安全专家Alex Hamerstone在接受CNN记者Erin Burnett采访时表示，最近一系列的航班停飞、美国联合航空公司、银行和微软的服务中断并非是单个不法分子的所为。

相反，TrustedSec的董事指出，人们越来越依赖于复杂的老旧系统，而公司“在推出之前不进行测试”。
